Entries.Text: Select a face to dress its character.
The body's sex is the face's, chosen in Viewport Filters.
Animation playback is not available for this game.
Select a face to preview animations on its character.
How the viewport shows the active face. None of these change the face's data.
How the face's parts are shaped in the viewport.
The body of the first character that uses this face, as listed in the References window. Male if no character uses it.
Shows the face on the male body.
Shows the face on the female body.
Saves the params. The FaceGen Editor edits the Param Editor's params, so this is the Param Editor's save.
The body the face is shown on in the viewport.
FaceGen Editor: could not load the shared face and hair textures (common_body).
Shapes the head, eyes, brows and beard by the face's sliders, as the game does. Off: the parts' base shapes.
FaceGen Editor: could not read the slider table {0}. Faces are shown in their base shape.
FaceGen Editor: could not read the FaceGen files of {0}. It is shown in its base shape.
{0} names no model, so {1} is shown.
The part model this field chooses. Only the values that name a model are listed; right-click for the Param Editor's field menu.
FaceGen Editor: {0} has no row {1}, or isn't a face param.
FaceGen Editor: could not read the FaceGen model from {0}. Shape and texture fields are shown by their internal names.
This project has no face params (FaceParam or FaceGenParam), or the Param Editor hasn't loaded them yet.
The face param shown. FaceParam is the one the game's characters use; FaceGenParam is the older kind, kept by this game from its predecessors.
Filters the faces by whether a character row (CharaInitParam's npcPlayerFaceGenId) points at them.
Adds a copy of the shown face (or of the first face) and shows it. It is placed as the Param Editor's duplicate options say (Duplicate in the context menu).
Select a face in the Faces window.
The Param Editor isn't loaded, and the FaceGen Editor edits its params.
The face shown. Right-click to open it in the Param Editor.
Shape and texture values are FaceGen sliders.
Shape and texture values are FaceGen mode coefficients.

FaceParam stores the value of each FaceGen slider (control), and the game builds the face from them in the character creator's order. FaceGenParam stores the 50 coefficients of the FaceGen model directly. In both, 128 is neutral.

Game value: {0} (byte {1})
The byte spans {2} to {3}. Ctrl+click to type a game value; the nearest byte is stored.

Byte: {0}
This field has no game value to show (a hidden slider, or a field without a FaceRangeParam range).
Vanilla has no face with this ID, so nothing is marked as changed and nothing can be reverted.
Copies every value of this group (whatever the field filter shows), to paste onto other faces.
Writes the copied group's values onto this face, as one undo step.
The group was copied from {0}: only the fields both params have are written.
Puts every field of this group back to the vanilla face's value, as one undo step.
Random values for the shown face (or every face selected in the list), or variations of it for crowds of NPCs. Each use is one undo step.
Where the FaceGen sliders move from. Amounts (gloss, makeup) and colours always move around the face's own values.
Small changes to the face's own values: a relative of this face.
The FaceGen sliders spread around neutral (128): a new face.
Hair, beard, brows, eyes and the like may change to another part that has a model. Stronger means more often.
Only the ticked groups change. Part IDs and flags never change, nor do sliders the character creator hides.
The same seed, face and settings give the same result. A new seed is drawn after each use.
Writes random values into the face (each selected face gets its own), as one undo step.
Copies of the shown face at the next free IDs, each changed around the face's own values by the settings above. Two undo steps: the copies, then their changes.
The copies are selected in the list afterwards, so they can be randomised again, assigned or deleted together.
Looks through the project's faces and the characters that wear them for things the game won't show as intended.
Character rows that point at a face that doesn't exist: the game shows them with no face, or a default one. Right-click one to make the face from the shown face.
Shows the character row in the Param Editor. Right-click to make the missing face.
Part fields whose value names no model: the game shows no part (for a head, the arrow shows the head drawn instead).
Notes: hidden sliders with unusual values ({0})

Sliders the character creator doesn't show, holding another value than most faces (in brackets). The game builds the face with them all the same; no face made in the creator would have them. Often deliberate for NPCs.
{0} of {1} faces are worn by no character.
Make Face {0} as a Copy of {1}
Make Face {0} (show a face to copy first)
Adds a copy of the face shown in the Properties window, with the ID the character points at and the character's name, and shows it. One undo step.
Gives this face to character rows (their npcPlayerFaceGenId), chosen in a list.
Characters point at the other face param, so this one's faces can't be worn.
Tick the characters that should wear face {0}, then Apply.
No param in this project has character rows that wear faces (npcPlayerFaceGenId).
Only characters that wear a face
Hides the rows with no face (npcPlayerFaceGenId below 0): characters that aren't player-like.
Faces saved as files: in the shared library (every project and game), the project's own, or anywhere. Faces from another game are fitted to this game's sliders.
Saves every field of the face, its FaceGen coefficients (so other games can rebuild it) and its colours as game values.
Saves the face into the chosen library under the name above. An existing file is never replaced: a number is added.
Saves the face to a file of your choice, to share it.
FaceGen Editor: saved the face to {0}
FaceGen Editor: could not save the face to {0}.
This project's own library (<project>\.smithbox\Faces), kept with the mod.
Click a face to import it. Faces from another game are marked in the warning colour.
Picks a face file from anywhere, to import.
Choose what to take from the file, then apply it to the shown face or add it as a new face.
From {0}: the shape is fitted to this game's sliders and the colours converted through their ranges. Parts aren't carried over.
From {0}: the shape is fitted to this param's sliders.
The FaceGen sliders (or modes), age, gender, caricature and asymmetry.
Skin, hair, eye and makeup colours, and amounts such as gloss and root darkness. From another game, through each field's game value.
Hair, beard, brows, eyes, head and the like.
Part numbers name other models in another game, so parts are only imported within a game.
Every other field (flags, body scales…). Only from the same game and param.
Writes the chosen parts of the file into the shown face, as one undo step.
Adds a copy of the shown face with the file's values written in, at the next free ID, named after the file, as one undo step.
Parts left as they are: the face is from {0}.
Other fields left as they are: the face is from another game or param.
Colours converted from {0}'s ranges. Skin colour means something different in some games (DS3 and BB add it; ER tints by it), so check it.
Shape not imported: the file or this game has no FaceGen model to rebuild it from.
Shape not imported: the file was made with a different FaceGen model.
Shape fitted from {0}: error {1} (0 is exact; a byte step is about 0.08).
Shape and texture fitted from {0}: errors {1} and {2} (0 is exact; a byte step is about 0.08).
This game's creator sliders can't make the face exactly (their ranges are narrower here), so the nearest face they can make was taken.
Nothing changed: the face already has these values.
Frames the head or the body, and looks at it from a preset angle.
Turns the camera slowly around the head (or the body, after Frame Body). It holds the camera while it is on.
The character rows that point at this face (CharaInitParam's npcPlayerFaceGenId): NPC players, invaders and the like.
Shows the row in the Param Editor.
Shows the row in the Param Editor. Right-click to preview the face in this character's outfit.
Dresses the viewport's character in this row's equipment (the Character Preview tool's CharaInitParam choice), so the face is seen with the helmet and hood masks it has in game.
Characters point at {0}, so no rows use the faces of this param.
These rows point at a face that doesn't exist. The arrow shows the face ID they name.
